# Cross-references and linking

> **这页管什么**：链接文字要能脱离上下文读懂；什么时候不该加链接。
>
> 来源：<https://developers.google.com/style/cross-references> · CC BY 4.0 · 本文件是**规则摘要**，非原文全文。

## Choosing when to link

- **Be selective — each link creates a decision for the reader, adding cognitive load.**
- Prefer providing context directly on the page over linking out, especially to define a term, briefly explain a concept, or give a couple of steps.
- Avoid duplicate links to the same destination within a page, except when linking to a specific section, when a page is very long, or when there are multiple entry points.
- Always link to the most relevant page and heading — don't provide multiple links serving the same purpose.
- For third-party standards or software, link out rather than fully documenting it.

## Writing link text

- Short, unique, descriptive — either the exact page title or a descriptive phrase capitalized as part of the sentence.
- **Front-load the important words.**
- Don't reuse identical link text for different destinations in the same document.
- Don't write lengthy link text such as a sentence or short paragraph.
- **Avoid vague text** — *this document*, *this article*, *click here*. Link text must stand alone.
- Don't use raw URLs as link text.
- Include both long form and abbreviation — "Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)".
- When linking a command-line flag or code-font element, include a description with the link unless awkward or redundant.

## Introducing links

- Use consistent phrasing: "For more information, see…" or "For more information about…, see…".
- Add an *about…* clause when the link text alone doesn't clarify relevance.
- Don't use *on* instead of *about*.
- **Use *see*** to refer readers to links.
- Make sure the context clarifies *why* the reader is being referred, without repeating the link text verbatim.

## Special behaviors

- For links that download files or open email clients, state that explicitly and note the file type in the link text.
- For links to sections, tell the reader clearly.
- **Don't force links to open in a new tab.** If unavoidable, note "(opens in a new tab)".
- Don't use external-link icons to indicate a different domain — state it in the text.

## Formatting

- Place punctuation immediately before or after link text, **outside** the link tags.
- Don't wrap linked cross-reference text in quotation marks.
- For unlinked references: quotation marks for document sections and short works, italics for full-length works.

## Navigation and styling

Avoid linking outside the documentation set from primary navigation. Ensure link text contrasts with body text, underline links only, and differentiate visited links accessibly.
